newsitem.title: USA: Pena wants plan to reduce U.S. oil imports.
newsitem.headline: Pena wants plan to reduce U.S. oil imports.

text.p: The United States needs a programme to reduce its dependence on imported energy, President Bill Clinton's choice for Energy secretary, Federico Pena, said on Thursday.

"I believe that we will not reverse our slide toward energy insecurity without a set of strategies that address both energy production and consumption and that are coupled with specific targets and timetables to measure performance," Pena said in prepared remarks for his confirmation hearing by the Senate Energy Committee.
Most committee sources said they expected the panel to approve Pena's nomination, but with some reservations.

"The critics have said your nomination is evidence the White House doesn't care about the department, that it was a 'throw away' position...," Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski said in prepared remarks.
Pena, Transportation secretary in Clinton's first term, was a late selection for Energy secretary and critics have questioned whether he has sufficient background in energy issues.
